searches: Michael Baumgartner AI extinction existential risk
Michael Baumgartner AI pause slowdown moratorium
Baumgartner congressman China AI agreement treaty

statements.venue: Op-ed in The Spokesman-Review, republished on his House site
statements.quote: But even if it were possible to stop AI (and it’s not), we should welcome the positive aspects which it can bring.
statements.context: Baumgartner arguing that America can win the AI race while making data centers pay their own electricity and water costs, and responding to people who oppose AI and data centers.
statements.reason: Promotes AI and says it cannot be stopped, but neither acknowledges nor dismisses catastrophic risk; the op-ed's concerns are electricity, water and costs.

statements.venue: Press release on introducing the Power and Water for Families Act (H.R.9419)
statements.quote: America must win the AI race, but working families should not be forced to subsidize it
statements.context: Baumgartner introducing a bill requiring large AI data centers to pay for the power and water infrastructure they need.
statements.reason: About data center costs and the AI race, which the rubric places at D.

statements.venue: Amendment text offered to Rules Committee Print 119-33 (Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act)
statements.quote: the increasing use of generative artificial intelligence by foreign adversaries may represent a national security risk, and the challenges posed by such use is not well understood
statements.context: Sense of Congress section of an amendment he offered requiring yearly State Department assessments of how foreign adversaries use generative AI, including to help develop chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons, and diplomatic steps to address it.
statements.reason: A general national security risk from adversaries' use of AI is D under ruling 4; the amendment only lists weapons misuse as a topic to assess rather than stating a catastrophic risk, so it sits at the D/C (misuse only) boundary.

slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing frontier AI for safety reasons.

pause.note: No statement found on pausing frontier AI; his July 2026 op-ed says AI cannot be stopped, but in the context of local opposition to data centers, not a safety pause.

intl.note: No statement found on coordinating with China on AI pacing. His June 2026 amendment calls for diplomacy on adversaries' malicious use of generative AI, not on the pace of frontier AI development, and his chip export control bill is about out-competing China.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Introduced H.R.5388, the American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act, to preempt state AI rules with a five-year moratorium on new state and local AI mandates.
Introduced the bipartisan MATCH Act to tighten export controls on chipmaking equipment to China.

Offered an amendment, the Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act, requiring yearly State Department assessments of foreign adversaries' malicious use of generative AI (including for chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons) and diplomatic steps to address it.
Introduced H.R.9419, the Power and Water for Families Act, requiring large AI data centers to pay for their own power and water infrastructure.
grade_reason: In 2025 and 2026 Baumgartner has spoken and legislated about AI (state preemption, the AI race with China, data center costs, adversaries' misuse of generative AI), but nothing found acknowledges or dismisses catastrophic risk from AI.
notes: All six required web searches ran in this attempt, plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors (7 in total); the earlier attempt, in which every search was refused, relied only on pages of baumgartner.house.gov. Searches on superintelligence, extinction, pause and 'AI safety' found nothing by this Michael Baumgartner. The two 2026 quotes were re-checked on the source pages this time. The new item is a June 2026 amendment he offered (Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act) to Rules Committee Print 119-33; a search summary called this the defense bill, which I did not confirm, and I did not find whether the amendment was made in order or adopted. Its quote is amendment text, not spoken words; line-break hyphens in the PDF were removed when copying. Reviewer: it lists AI help with chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons by adversaries as a topic to assess; I graded it D (ruling 4, general national security risk) with 'boundary', but a reviewer could treat it as C with 'misuse_only'. The 2025 H.R.5388 press release was dropped from statements to stay within three D statements and remains in record. No source shows him sponsoring or co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R.10538); cosponsor lists seen name only Democrats and Reps. Whitesides and Moran, but I did not check congress.gov directly. The July 2026 op-ed line 'even if it were possible to stop AI (and it’s not)' was graded D, not F, and pause 'none', because it responds to local opposition to AI and data centers and does not address catastrophic risk or a safety pause. A Ripon Society item on his 2025 trip to Beijing with Rep. Adam Smith was not opened; the search summary described it as about China relations generally, not AI.
